The proposed answer of 1 is incorrect.

The problem says the new bound refines the earlier bound $n \le 2m-3$. Take $k=3$ in the proposed form. With $c=1$, the bound becomes $n \le 2m - \lfloor 4/2 \rfloor = 2m-2$, which is weaker than $2m-3$, so it cannot be a refinement. For the new bound to be at least as strong at $k=3$, we need $\lfloor (3+c)/2 \rfloor \ge 3$, which requires $c \ge 3$. The value $c=3$ gives exactly $2m - \lfloor (k+3)/2 \rfloor$, which equals $2m-3$ at $k=3$ and decreases as $k$ grows. This matches the form of a refinement, and I recall the intersecting rank-metric code literature stating this bound with $c=3$, though I did not verify the source here.
